## Grammatik

```yaml grammar
- id: akkusativ-fixture
  title: "Akkusativ, fixture"
  cefr: A1.1
  skillTags: [case.akkusativ, article.definite]
  difficulty: 2
  rule: |
    Only the masculine article changes in the Akkusativ.
  pattern: |
    Subjekt + Verb + Akkusativobjekt
  tables:
    - caption: "Bestimmter Artikel"
      columns: ["Kasus", "maskulin", "feminin", "neutrum", "Plural"]
      rows:
        - ["Nominativ", "der", "die", "das", "die"]
        - ["Akkusativ", "den", "die", "das", "die"]
      highlight: [[1, 1]]
      highlightNote: "The only cell that changes."
  examples:
    - de: "Ich sehe den Tisch."
      en: "I see the table."
      cases: [{ text: "Ich", case: NOM }, { text: "den Tisch", case: AKK }]
      note: "sehen takes an Akkusativ object."
    - de: "Ich will den Tisch kaufen."
      en: "I want to buy the table."
      satzklammer: { position2: "will", ende: "kaufen" }
    - de: "Ich fahre morgen wegen der Arbeit schnell nach Berlin."
      en: "Tomorrow I am driving to Berlin quickly because of work."
      tekamolo:
        - { text: "morgen", slot: temporal }
        - { text: "wegen der Arbeit", slot: kausal }
        - { text: "schnell", slot: modal }
        - { text: "nach Berlin", slot: lokal }
  contrast: |
    Compare with the Nominativ, where der stays der.
  commonMistakes:
    - wrong: "Ich sehe der Tisch."
      right: "Ich sehe den Tisch."
      why: "Masculine changes to den in the Akkusativ."
  tips:
    - "Only masculine changes."
  memoryHook: "den is the only one with an n."
  relatedIds: [2098-12-31-lektion-98:grammar:nominativ]
```

## Unterrichtsarbeit

```yaml classwork
- id: cw-fill-blank
  type: fill_blank
  prompt: "Ich sehe ___ Tisch."
  answer: ["den"]
  accept: ["den"]
  solution: "Ich sehe den Tisch."
  why: "Masculine becomes den in the Akkusativ."
  takeaway: "der becomes den."
  skillTags: [case.akkusativ]
  difficulty: 1
  points: 1

- id: cw-mcq
  type: mcq
  prompt: "Ich sehe ___ Tisch."
  given: { options: ["der", "den", "dem", "das"] }
  answer: "den"
  solution: "den"
  why: "Tisch is masculine and is the direct object."
  takeaway: "Masculine is the only gender that changes."
  skillTags: [case.akkusativ]

- id: cw-multi-select
  type: multi_select
  prompt: "Which articles are masculine Akkusativ?"
  given: { options: ["den", "die", "das", "einen"] }
  answer: ["den", "einen"]
  solution: "den, einen"
  why: "Both are the masculine Akkusativ forms."
  takeaway: "den and einen mark the masculine object."
  skillTags: [article.definite, article.indefinite]

- id: cw-true-false
  type: true_false
  prompt: "Neuter articles change in the Akkusativ."
  answer: false
  solution: "false"
  why: "Neuter is identical in Nominativ and Akkusativ."
  takeaway: "Only masculine changes."
  skillTags: [case.akkusativ]

- id: cw-match
  type: match
  prompt: "Match the article to its gender."
  given:
    left: ["der", "die", "das"]
    right: ["maskulin", "feminin", "neutrum"]
  answer: [["der", "maskulin"], ["die", "feminin"], ["das", "neutrum"]]
  solution: "der = maskulin, die = feminin, das = neutrum"
  why: "These are the three definite articles."
  takeaway: "Three genders, three articles."
  skillTags: [noun.gender]
  points: 3

- id: cw-order-words
  type: order_words
  prompt: "Bilde einen Satz."
  given:
    tokens: ["morgen", "ich", "nach Berlin", "fahre"]
  answer: ["Ich fahre morgen nach Berlin."]
  accept: ["Morgen fahre ich nach Berlin."]
  solution: "Ich fahre morgen nach Berlin."
  why: "The conjugated verb takes position 2."
  takeaway: "Position 2 belongs to the conjugated verb."
  skillTags: [wordorder.v2]
  difficulty: 2

- id: cw-translate-de-en
  type: translate_de_en
  prompt: "Übersetze: Ich sehe den Tisch."
  answer: ["I see the table."]
  solution: "I see the table."
  why: "sehen is to see and den Tisch is the object."
  takeaway: "German has no continuous tense."
  skillTags: [case.akkusativ]

- id: cw-translate-en-de
  type: translate_en_de
  prompt: "Translate: I see the table."
  answer: ["Ich sehe den Tisch."]
  solution: "Ich sehe den Tisch."
  why: "The table is the direct object, so der becomes den."
  takeaway: "Objects take the Akkusativ."
  skillTags: [case.akkusativ]

- id: cw-transform
  type: transform
  prompt: "Verneine: Das ist ein Tisch."
  answer: ["Das ist kein Tisch."]
  solution: "Das ist kein Tisch."
  why: "nicht plus ein always collapses into kein."
  takeaway: "ein becomes kein."
  skillTags: [negation.kein]

- id: cw-conjugate
  type: conjugate
  prompt: "Konjugiere gehen."
  given:
    infinitive: gehen
    persons: [ich, du, er, wir, ihr, sie]
  answer:
    ich: gehe
    du: gehst
    er: geht
    wir: gehen
    ihr: geht
    sie: gehen
  solution: "ich gehe, du gehst, er geht, wir gehen, ihr geht, sie gehen"
  why: "gehen is regular in the present tense."
  takeaway: "Regular verbs take -e -st -t -en -t -en."
  skillTags: [verb.praesens.regular]
  points: 6

- id: cw-gender-pick
  type: gender_pick
  prompt: "___ Tisch"
  given: { options: ["der", "die", "das"] }
  answer: "der"
  solution: "der Tisch"
  why: "Tisch is masculine."
  takeaway: "Learn the article with the noun."
  skillTags: [noun.gender]

- id: cw-case-pick
  type: case_pick
  prompt: "Which case is 'den Tisch' in 'Ich sehe den Tisch'?"
  given: { options: ["NOM", "AKK", "DAT", "GEN"] }
  answer: "AKK"
  solution: "AKK"
  why: "It is the thing directly affected by the verb."
  takeaway: "The direct object is Akkusativ."
  skillTags: [case.akkusativ]

- id: cw-short-answer
  type: short_answer
  prompt: "Wie heißt du?"
  answer: ["Ich heiße Nabi."]
  accept: ["Ich heisse Nabi."]
  solution: "Ich heiße Nabi."
  why: "heißen is the standard verb for stating a name."
  takeaway: "Ich heiße plus your name."
  skillTags: [phrase.redemittel]

- id: cw-dialogue
  type: dialogue
  prompt: "Antworte: Woher kommst du?"
  answer: ["Ich komme aus Pakistan."]
  solution: "Ich komme aus Pakistan."
  why: "woher asks origin, and the answer uses aus."
  takeaway: "woher is answered with aus."
  skillTags: [phrase.redemittel, question.wfragen]

- id: cw-listening
  type: listening
  prompt: "Schreibe, was du hörst."
  given: { audioText: "Der Tisch ist neu." }
  answer: ["Der Tisch ist neu."]
  solution: "Der Tisch ist neu."
  why: "The sentence uses the Nominativ because ist links two Nominativ parts."
  takeaway: "sein never produces an Akkusativ."
  skillTags: [pronunciation]

- id: cw-four-forms
  type: four_forms
  prompt: "Give this sentence in all four shapes."
  given:
    base_en: "He is the engineer."
  answer:
    A: "Er ist der Ingenieur."
    N: "Er ist nicht der Ingenieur."
    I: "Ist er der Ingenieur?"
    IN: "Ist er nicht der Ingenieur?"
  solution: "Er ist der Ingenieur. / Er ist nicht der Ingenieur. / Ist er der Ingenieur? / Ist er nicht der Ingenieur?"
  why: |
    The verb stays in position 2 for the two statements and moves to position 1 for the two questions. nicht negates the definite article, and it sits directly in front of what it negates.
  takeaway: "One sentence, four shapes: statement, negative, question, negative question."
  skillTags: [wordorder.v2, question.janein, negation.nicht]
  difficulty: 3
  points: 4

- id: cw-cloze
  type: cloze
  prompt: "Ich ___ nach Hause und ___ den Tisch."
  answer: ["gehe", "sehe"]
  solution: "Ich gehe nach Hause und sehe den Tisch."
  why: "Both verbs take the ich ending -e."
  takeaway: "ich always ends in -e in the present tense."
  skillTags: [verb.praesens.regular]
  points: 2
```

## Hausaufgaben

```yaml homework
- id: hw-01
  type: translate_en_de
  prompt: "Translate: I am reading the book."
  answer: ["Ich lese das Buch."]
  accept: ["Ich lese gerade das Buch."]
  dueDate: 2099-01-08
  points: 2
  revealPolicy: on_request
  hints:
    - level: 1
      text: "German has no continuous tense."
    - level: 2
      text: "The verb is lesen and its du and er forms are irregular."
    - level: 3
      text: "Buch is neuter, so the article does not change."
  solution: "Ich lese das Buch."
  why: "Neuter is identical in the Nominativ and the Akkusativ."
  takeaway: "Do not force an ending change where the gender has none."
  skillTags: [case.akkusativ, verb.praesens.irregular]
  grammarRefs: [akkusativ-fixture]
  difficulty: 2

- id: hw-02
  type: fill_blank
  prompt: "Ich kaufe ___ Tisch."
  answer: ["den"]
  dueDate: 2099-01-08
  revealPolicy: after_due
  solution: "Ich kaufe den Tisch."
  why: "kaufen takes a direct object."
  takeaway: "der becomes den after a transitive verb."
  skillTags: [case.akkusativ]
```
